Both mood and device targets were screened and deliberately NOT authored. Rank order follows the located evidence strength, not symptom prominence: the stroke edge is ranked second despite being the highest-consequence outcome because its three anchors are the largest designs in the file, while the dizziness edge is ranked LAST because its primary anchor is a single-arm treatment-response study whose authors expressly disclaim causation.

Classification guard: all three edges assert documented association only, with the bidirectional atrial fibrillation relationship (PMID 37023861) and the negative pacing-minimisation trial result (PMID 37638973) recorded on the face of the edge, so neither the rhythm edge nor its target may be read as a one-directional causal route.

The dizziness edge carries a required excluded-differential workup, because the located case report shows a concurrent sleep apnoea-hypopnoea syndrome accounting for the same symptoms and changing management away from pacemaker implantation (PMID 19156381). Do not attribute dizziness to sinus node disease without a documented sleep apnoea assessment and a medication review.

The stroke edge requires documented atrial fibrillation status and a documented CHA2DS2-VASC score for any individual claim, because the located cohort shows the association is concentrated in patients scoring 2 or less (HR 2.13) and is not significant above that (PMID 41317944), and the located meta-analysis names whether anticoagulation helps in this population as an open question rather than an answered one (PMID 37977871).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Sick sinus syndrome and atrial fibrillation are the two poles of a documented tachy-bradyarrhythmia, and three independent designs report the association from different directions. A systematic review and meta-analysis of 35 articles covering 37,550 patients found patients with sick sinus syndrome were associated with NEW-ONSET ATRIAL FIBRILLATION compared with those without, and reports the relationship as BIDIRECTIONAL, with atrial fibrillation risk varying by pacing strategy (VVI/VVIR carrying higher new-onset atrial fibrillation risk than DDD/DDDR, while AAI/AAIR versus DDD/DDDR showed no significant difference) (PMID 37023861). A nationwide randomised controlled trial of 540 patients with sinus node dysfunction and an indication for first pacemaker implantation found the primary endpoint of atrial fibrillation longer than 6 minutes occurred in 46 PERCENT of patients, with no difference between pacing strategies (hazard ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.76-1.25, P = .83), and no difference in atrial fibrillation exceeding 6 or 24 hours, persistent atrial fibrillation, or cardioversions (PMID 37638973). A literature review of atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response names sick sinus syndrome among the significant contributors to its development, alongside atrioventricular nodal block and medication effects, and describes the pathophysiology as complex electrical and structural REMODELLING OF THE ATRIA that produces bradycardia and symptomatic conduction delays (PMID 40607080). Recorded as documented association only, with the near-half-prevalence atrial fibrillation figure in a pacemaker-indication cohort explicitly framed as reflecting a population already selected for advanced sinus node disease rather than a community rate.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the located evidence describes a shared substrate rather than a one-directional cause. The meta-analysis describes the sick sinus syndrome and atrial fibrillation relationship as bidirectional and does not establish which precedes which (PMID 37023861). The randomised trial enrolled patients who ALREADY had an indication for first pacemaker implantation, so its 46 percent atrial fibrillation endpoint describes an advanced-disease population, and it is a NEGATIVE trial for the pacing intervention, finding that atrial pacing minimisation did NOT reduce atrial fibrillation incidence, which argues against the simple hypothesis that excess atrial pacing is the driver. The literature review supplies a plausible unifying mechanism, atrial electrical and structural remodelling, but states it as the pathophysiology of the overlap rather than as a demonstrated causal sequence from sinus node disease to atrial fibrillation (PMID 40607080). Individual claims require a dated diagnosis of sick sinus syndrome, objective evidence of the atrial arrhythmia on a dated tracing or monitoring record, and a clinical determination of which condition is temporally antecedent, because the two are frequently recorded together as tachy-bradyarrhythmia rather than as one producing the other, and because pacing strategy, which the located evidence shows materially affects atrial fibrillation risk, is itself a treatment variable rather than a fixed feature of the disease.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is age-related fibroelastic replacement of the sinus node and atrioventricular conduction tissue, which slows impulse formation and conduction and produces the bradycardic pole, with the same degenerative process extending to the atrial myocardium as electrical and structural remodelling that lowers the threshold for reentrant atrial fibrillation and produces the tachycardic pole. The mechanism is named as a shared degenerative substrate rather than a causal sequence because the located evidence reports a bidirectional relationship and a remodelling association, and does not establish that sinus node degeneration produces atrial remodelling rather than both reflecting a common ageing substrate, which is also why the located review describes the overlap in terms of age-related degeneration of the cardiac conduction system.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at meta-analytic, randomised-controlled-trial, and literature-review class, following the file's existing cardiovascular pathway scope. The meta-analysis is the anchor that supplies the pooled direction of travel and the explicit bidirectionality statement together with the pacing-strategy gradient, which is the located evidence that atrial fibrillation burden in this population is at least partly treatment-dependent (PMID 37023861). The randomised trial is the anchor that supplies the 46 percent atrial fibrillation prevalence in a defined cohort and, more importantly, serves as an EXPLICIT COUNTERWEIGHT, because it is a negative trial showing that reducing atrial pacing did not reduce atrial fibrillation, so the mechanism cannot be stated as simple pacing-induced (PMID 37638973). The literature review supplies the remodelling mechanism and the named co-contributors that must be excluded (PMID 40607080). Because the evidence is bidirectional and partly confounded by the very treatment these patients receive, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, records the negative trial on the face of the edge, and requires a temporal determination before any individual attribution.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The primary anchor is a meta-analysis of observational studies and reports heterogeneity across included therapy comparisons without a pooled effect size for the core new-onset atrial fibrillation claim (PMID 37023861). The randomised trial is a NEGATIVE trial, its null result argues against the pacing-exposure mechanism, and its population is restricted to patients with a first pacemaker indication, so it cannot be read as a community prevalence of atrial fibrillation in sick sinus syndrome (PMID 37638973). The third anchor is a literature review rather than primary data (PMID 40607080). NO located anchor establishes temporal order between the two diagnoses in an unselected individual, and the located evidence shows pacing mode itself changes atrial fibrillation risk, so any individual claim must separate disease effect from treatment effect. The syncope route was withheld as EVIDENCE-INSUFFICIENT because the located anchors address syncope as a safety endpoint of pacing programming or as a symptom of a different physiology, and no anchor quantifies syncope as a complication of sinus node disease itself. The implantable-cardiac-pacemaker route was withheld as TREATMENT-CONSEQUENCE rather than a medical secondary condition, the located evidence being entirely about implantation decisions and outcomes.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Sinus node dysfunction carries an elevated ischaemic stroke risk that three large designs quantify, and they do so in complementary populations that together cover both the AF-free and the AF-positive patient. A systematic review and meta-analysis of 6 studies with 106,163 patients found an average yearly stroke incidence of 1.542 PERCENT (95% CI 1.334 to 1.749) in sinus node dysfunction, and found the incidence SIMILAR between isolated sinus node dysfunction (1.587 percent, 95% CI 1.510 to 1.664) and non-isolated sinus node dysfunction with atrial fibrillation (1.660 percent, 95% CI 0.705 to 2.615), with atrial fibrillation (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.01 to 2.33), prior stroke or transient ischaemic attack or other thrombotic events (HR 2.54, 95% CI 1.14 to 5.69), hypertension (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.11 to 2.07) and heart failure (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.97) associated with stroke in that population (PMID 37977871). A UK Biobank analysis of 451,493 participants followed for a median 13.2 years found yearly ischaemic stroke incidence of 0.37 percent in isolated sinus node dysfunction, 0.60 percent in combined sinus node dysfunction and atrial fibrillation, 0.59 percent in isolated atrial fibrillation and 0.10 percent in controls, with ISOLATED SINUS NODE DYSFUNCTION CONFERRING A SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED RISK compared with controls (subdistribution hazard ratio 2.28, 95% CI 1.57-3.31, P < .001) while combined sinus node dysfunction and atrial fibrillation carried a risk similar to isolated atrial fibrillation (subdistribution hazard ratio 1.07, 95% CI 0.84-1.37, P = .58), which the authors interpret as evidence for a left atrial myopathy in patients with isolated sinus node dysfunction (PMID 40315941). A hospital-based cohort of 24,960 patients with atrial fibrillation, of whom 1,624 had sick sinus syndrome and a pacemaker, found stroke incidence of 4.02 percent per patient-year in the sick sinus syndrome group versus 3.03 percent in the non-sick-sinus-syndrome group (P < .001), with sick sinus syndrome independently associated with a 23 PERCENT higher stroke risk (HR 1.23, 95% CI 1.10-1.37) that was STRONGEST IN PATIENTS WITH LOW CHA2DS2-VASC SCORES (HR 2.13, 95% CI 1.76-2.58) and not significant in those with scores above 2 (HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.89-1.17, P = .722) (PMID 41317944). Recorded as documented association only, with the residual, the subdistribution, and the confounding-by-indication structure of each design carried on the face of the edge.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the located evidence is a risk-marker relationship rather than a demonstrated embolic mechanism. The meta-analysis reports a similar stroke incidence in isolated sinus node dysfunction and in sinus node dysfunction with atrial fibrillation, and its own conclusion is that patients with sinus node dysfunction carry a SIMILAR RISK of stroke to those with combined sinus node dysfunction and atrial fibrillation, with future studies needed to investigate whether stroke-prevention interventions such as anticoagulation can help (PMID 37977871), which is an explicit statement that the mechanism and the intervention are unresolved. The UK Biobank analysis is observational and interprets its finding through a proposed left atrial myopathy rather than a demonstrated one, and it deliberately excludes prosthetic heart valves, rheumatic mitral valve disease, mitral stenosis and prior ischaemic stroke, so its estimate applies to a comparatively lower-risk population (PMID 40315941). The Taiwanese cohort is HOSPITAL-BASED and defines sick sinus syndrome STRICTLY as symptomatic sinus node dysfunction requiring pacemaker implantation, so it is confounded by indication: the patients with sick sinus syndrome were older, more often female, and had higher CHADS2 and CHA2DS2-VASc scores, and after CHA2DS2-VASc adjustment the association was strongest precisely where the score was lowest, which is the signature of a risk marker adding information beyond standard stroke-risk stratification rather than of an independent embolic cause (PMID 41317944). Individual claims require a dated diagnosis of sinus node dysfunction, a dated ischaemic stroke event with imaging or equivalent objective confirmation, a documented atrial fibrillation status, and a documented CHA2DS2-VASc score, because the located evidence shows the strength of this association depends on both the AF status and the baseline stroke score, and because no located anchor establishes that anticoagulation prevents stroke in sinus node dysfunction without atrial fibrillation.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is thromboembolic stroke arising from an atrial substrate shared with the sinus node disorder, in which the same age-related fibrotic and remodelling process that slows sinus node impulse formation also alters atrial architecture, creating stasis, appendicular flow reduction and an arrhythmogenic substrate that permits thrombus formation and embolisation to the cerebral circulation. The vector is named as a shared atrial substrate rather than a direct sinus-to-brain pathway because the located evidence reports the association in patients with ISOLATED sinus node dysfunction without atrial fibrillation, which is what the UK Biobank analysis interprets as evidence for a left atrial myopathy, and because a thromboembolic mechanism cannot be assumed in the absence of demonstrated atrial thrombus or appendicular stasis in any given individual.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at meta-analytic, prospective-population-cohort, and hospital-based-cohort class, following the file's existing cardiovascular pathway scope. The meta-analysis is the anchor that supplies the pooled annual stroke incidence of 1.542 percent and, critically, the finding that ISOLATED sinus node dysfunction and sinus node dysfunction with atrial fibrillation carry a similar risk, which is what prevents this edge from collapsing into the already-registered atrial fibrillation route (PMID 37977871). The UK Biobank analysis is the anchor that supplies the large-population effect estimate (subdistribution hazard ratio 2.28) and the explicit left atrial myopathy interpretation that motivates the mechanism category, and its deliberate exclusion of prior stroke and valvular disease is what makes the estimate a clean signal rather than a restatement of baseline risk (PMID 40315941). The Taiwanese cohort is registered as the EXPLICIT COUNTERWEIGHT and as the source of the most clinically actionable nuance: it shows the association is concentrated in patients whose CHA2DS2-VASC score is low, which is precisely the population standard risk stratification would not flag, and it does so in a hospital-based sample with a strict pacemaker-requiring definition of sick sinus syndrome (PMID 41317944). Because the design is confounding-by-indication throughout, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, requires documented AF status and a documented CHA2DS2-VASC score, and states the unresolved anticoagulation question in the causation status rather than implying an established preventive.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The primary anchor pools only 6 studies and its atrial fibrillation subgroup confidence interval is wide and includes values from 0.705 to 2.615 percent, so the isolated-versus-combined similarity finding rests on imprecise data (PMID 37977871). The UK Biobank analysis had only 593 participants with ISOLATED sinus node dysfunction, so the headline subdistribution hazard ratio of 2.28 rests on a small exposed group within a very large cohort and is derived from ICD-coded registry linkage rather than adjudicated clinical diagnosis (PMID 40315941). The third anchor is hospital-based, defines sick sinus syndrome as requiring pacemaker implantation, and the exposed group is confounded by age, sex and baseline stroke score, with the association attenuating to non-significance in patients with CHA2DS2-VASC scores above 2 (PMID 41317944). NO located anchor demonstrates atrial thrombus, appendicular flow stasis, or a mechanism of embolisation in any individual, and NO located anchor tests whether anticoagulation reduces stroke in sinus node dysfunction without atrial fibrillation, which the meta-analysis itself names as future work. The cardiac-arrhythmia route is a chain rather than a duplicate and is authored separately, and the fact that the two atrial fibrillation cohorts report higher absolute stroke incidence than the isolated-dysfunction cohort is a population-composition difference rather than a contradiction.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter as the coexisting tachycardic pole, since the located evidence separates isolated from combined disease and the combined group carries a similar or higher absolute risk
Left atrial appendicular thrombus and appendicular flow stasis, the intermediate steps a thromboembolic mechanism would require and which no located anchor demonstrates
Hypertension, heart failure, and prior stroke or transient ischaemic attack, each independently associated with stroke in the located meta-analysis at hazard ratios between 1.41 and 2.54
Anticoagulation status, since the located meta-analysis identifies whether stroke-prevention interventions help in this population as an open question rather than an answered one

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Dizziness and near-syncope are the characteristic symptoms of symptomatic sinus node disease, and the located evidence quantifies them in a cohort where symptom burden falls sharply with treatment. A prospective study of 87 elderly patients (mean age 75.4 years, 51 percent women) with sinus node dysfunction and an indication for cardiac pacing found that FEWER PATIENTS HAD SYNCOPE (4 versus 45 percent) AND DIZZINESS AFTER PERMANENT PACEMAKER IMPLANTATION (12 versus 45 percent) compared with the 12 months before, with falls reduced from 53 to 15 percent of patients and falls leading to fracture from 8 to 0 percent, while noting that no causal relationship could be established due to the study design (PMID 27702858). A review of closed-loop stimulation pacemakers describes sinus node dysfunction as a condition that can cause symptoms INCLUDING FATIGUE, DIZZINESS, OR FAINTING, and notes that closed-loop stimulation has shown promise in preventing fainting episodes caused by vasovagal syncope, a distinct physiology it attributes to the device rather than to the disease (PMID 40388576). A case report of a patient with symptomatic sinus bradycardia and second-degree sinoatrial block with Wenckebach periodicity presented with dizziness and near syncope, and is notable for a DIFFERENTIAL FINDING: the pacemaker decision was altered in favour of nasal continuous positive airway pressure because a severe mixed sleep apnoea-hypopnoea syndrome was diagnosed (PMID 19156381). Recorded as documented association only, with the before-and-after symptom figures expressly attributed to treatment rather than to disease course.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the strongest anchor is fundamentally a treatment-response study, not an incidence study. The cohort study is a single-arm before-and-after design in patients who all received a pacemaker, and its authors state explicitly that NO CAUSAL RELATIONSHIP COULD BE ESTABLISHED DUE TO THE STUDY DESIGN (PMID 27702858); the 45 percent to 12 percent dizziness change therefore cannot be read as a disease-attributable symptom rate, and the reduction is equally consistent with the elimination of symptomatic bradycardia, with the placebo and regression-to-the-mean effects of an invasive procedure, and with the natural fluctuation of a subjective symptom. The closed-loop stimulation review is authored in part by pacemaker-manufacturer employees and describes a device intervention in a mixed population that also includes vasovagal syncope, which is a different autonomic physiology rather than sinus node disease (PMID 40388576). The case report is single-patient class and its own lesson cuts against a simple attribution, because the same patient's dizziness and near syncope were substantially explained by a concurrent sleep apnoea-hypopnoea syndrome and the pacing decision was changed accordingly (PMID 19156381). Individual claims require a dated diagnosis of sinus node dysfunction, a contemporaneous dated report of dizziness with documented temporal relationship to documented bradyarrhythmia or sinoatrial block, a documented sleep apnoea assessment, and a review of rate-limiting and AV-nodal blocking medications, because the located case report shows an alternative diagnosis changing the management entirely, and because the target identity already carries registered edges from two other cardiovascular causes including one sinus-node sibling.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is episodic cerebral hypoperfusion during pauses in sinus node impulse formation or sinoatrial conduction block, so that a period of bradycardia or asystole produces a transient drop in cardiac output and therefore in cerebral perfusion, which the patient experiences as lightheadedness, disorientation or near-syncope, and which, when prolonged or recurrent, produces falls with injury or fracture. The vector is named as a haemodynamic consequence of the same degenerative process that produces the bradycardia rather than as a separate neurological lesion, because the located evidence attributes the symptom to the pacing-sensitive bradycardia rather than to any structural brain change, and the same anchors require that sleep apnoea and medication effect be excluded first, since both can produce identical symptoms without any cerebral hypoperfusion.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at cohort, narrative-review, and case-report class, following the file's existing cardiovascular pathway scope. The cohort study is the anchor that supplies the quantitative symptom burden, dizziness in 45 percent of patients before implantation and 12 percent after, together with the falls and fracture figures and the authors' own statement that no causal relationship could be established (PMID 27702858). The closed-loop stimulation review is the anchor that supplies the plain statement of the symptom triad and the chronotropic-incompetence framing, and its manufacturer-affiliations are disclosed as a source-quality caveat rather than suppressed (PMID 40388576). The case report is registered as the EXPLICIT COUNTERWEIGHT and as the source of the differential requirement, because it is the located evidence that a competing diagnosis, sleep apnoea-hypopnoea syndrome, can account for the same symptoms and can change the management, which is why the target identity also carries a registered edge from a sleep-related condition elsewhere in the graph and why sleep apnoea screening is named as a prerequisite rather than an afterthought (PMID 19156381). Because the primary anchor measures response to treatment rather than disease incidence, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, quotes the authors' causal disclaimer in the causation status, and requires an excluded-differential workup before any individual attribution.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The primary anchor is a single-arm before-and-after study of 87 patients with no control group, in which every patient received a pacemaker, so the 45 percent to 12 percent dizziness change cannot be separated into disease effect, treatment effect, and natural history, and the authors state this limitation themselves (PMID 27702858). The second anchor is a narrative review authored in part by employees of the device manufacturer whose product is under discussion, and its population mixes sinus node dysfunction with vasovagal syncope, a different autonomic physiology (PMID 40388576). The third anchor is a SINGLE-PATIENT case report from 2008 and is the weakest source class in this edge (PMID 19156381). NO located anchor reports the incidence of dizziness or presyncope attributable to sinus node dysfunction in an unselected, untreated population, because the located evidence is drawn almost entirely from patients referred for pacing, and no located anchor establishes a dose-response between the depth or duration of bradycardic pauses and symptom severity. This edge is also ranked BELOW the cardiac-arrhythmia and stroke edges despite being more immediately symptomatic, because the located evidence for it is the weakest class in the file: the disorder's symptom profile is well described, but the quantitative attribution of those symptoms to the disease rather than to its treatment, to sleep apnoea, or to medication is precisely what the anchors decline to establish.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Sleep apnoea-hypopnoea syndrome, which the located case report shows can account for the same dizziness and near-syncope in a patient with documented sinus bradycardia and second-degree sinoatrial block, and which changed the management away from pacemaker implantation

Medication effect from rate-limiting and AV-nodal blocking drugs, a reversible bradycardia cause that the located review names and that must be excluded before attributing symptoms to the conduction disease

Orthostatic hypotension and other cardiovascular causes of dizziness, which the target identity already carries from two other registered causes and which must be separated by documented positional relationship
Reflex or vasovagal syncope, a different autonomic physiology that the located device review explicitly separates from sinus node dysfunction and that must not be folded into this edge

suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because dizziness is the presenting symptom that most often brings sinus node disease to clinical attention, because it is quantified at 45 percent in a paced cohort, and because the target identity had only two registered incoming edges, neither from a conduction-system disorder. The conservative framing is unusually explicit about its own weakness: the primary anchor is a treatment-response study whose authors disclaim causation, the second carries manufacturer affiliations, the third is a single case report, and the edge is ranked below two better-anchored edges in the same file for that reason rather than being presented as the headline claim.

sourceReferences.citation: Brenner R, Ammann P, Yoon SI, et al. Reduction of falls and fractures after permanent pacemaker implantation in elderly patients with sinus node dysfunction. Europace. 2017 Jul 1;19(7):1220-1226. doi: 10.1093/europace/euw156. PMID 27702858.
sourceReferences.note: Prospective study of 87 elderly patients (mean age 75.4 years, 51% women) with sinus node dysfunction and an indication for cardiac pacing, examined by standardized interview for fall history over 12 months before and after permanent pacemaker implantation, finding the proportion of patients experiencing at least one fall reduced by 71% (from 53 to 15%, P < 0.001), falls with injury reduced (28 versus 10%, P = 0.005), falls requiring medical attention reduced (31 versus 8%, P < 0.001), falls leading to fracture reduced (8 versus 0%, P = 0.013), and fewer patients having syncope (4 versus 45%, P < 0.001) and dizziness (12 versus 45%, P < 0.001) after implantation, while stating that although permanent pacemaker implantation is associated with a significantly reduced risk of these adverse events, no causal relationship could be established due to the study design.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: Europace. 2017;19(7):1220-1226. Prospective single-arm before-and-after study, 87 patients with sinus node dysfunction and pacing indication, mean age 75.4 (SD 8.3) years, 51% women; abstract states PPM implantation was associated with a reduced proportion of patients experiencing at least one fall by 71% (from 53 to 15%, P < 0.001), fewer patients had syncope (4 vs 45%, P < 0.001) and dizziness (12 vs 45%, P < 0.001), and that no causal relationship could be established due to the study design.

sourceReferences.citation: Gargaro A, Biancalana G, Botto GL, et al. The clinical role of closed loop stimulation pacemakers in the treatment of patients with sinus node dysfunction: a review. Future Cardiol. 2025 Jun;21(8):567-578. doi: 10.1080/14796678.2025.2507464. PMID 40388576.
sourceReferences.note: Review of the clinical role of closed-loop stimulation pacemakers in sinus node dysfunction, stating that sinus node dysfunction disrupts the heart's natural rhythm, CAN CAUSE SYMPTOMS LIKE FATIGUE, DIZZINESS, OR FAINTING and is often treated with pacemakers, describing the device's use for chronotropic incompetence in which patients have difficulty increasing heart rate during activity, and reporting that closed-loop stimulation has shown promise in preventing fainting episodes caused by vasovagal syncope and in preventing atrial fibrillation detected by implanted devices. DISCLOSED CONFLICT OF INTEREST: two authors are employees of the device manufacturer whose product is under discussion, and one further author reports speaker fees from three other device manufacturers.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: Future Cardiol. 2025;21(8):567-578. Narrative review of closed-loop stimulation pacemakers in sinus node dysfunction; abstract states SND can cause symptoms like fatigue, dizziness, or fainting and is often treated with pacemakers, that CLS addresses chronotropic incompetence, and that CLS has shown promise in preventing fainting episodes caused by vasovagal syncope and in preventing device-detected atrial fibrillation. Conflict of interest statement declares two authors are employees of the closed-loop stimulation pacemaker manufacturer.

sourceReferences.citation: Lotze U, Rothhagen B, Neubauer K, et al. Dizziness and near syncope due to sinus bradycardia and sinoatrial block associated with obesity and daytime tiredness. A clear indication for pacemaker implantation?. Herz. 2008 Sep;33(6):455-9. doi: 10.1007/s00059-008-3096-2. PMID 19156381.
sourceReferences.note: Case report of a patient with symptomatic sinus bradycardia and second-degree sinoatrial block with Wenckebach periodicity presenting with dizziness and near syncope, in whom the primary decision to implant a pacemaker was altered in favour of treatment with nasal continuous positive airway pressure because a severe mixed sleep apnoea-hypopnoea syndrome was diagnosed on careful evaluation of history and symptoms, concluding that on diagnosing sleep apnoea-hypopnoea syndrome with an obstructive component in patients with symptomatic bradycardia and sinoatrial block there is no primary need for a pacemaker.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: Herz. 2008;33(6):455-459. Single-patient case report; abstract states the case describes a patient with symptomatic sinus bradycardia and second-degree SA block with Wenckebach periodicity in whom the primary decision to implant a pacemaker was altered in favour of treatment with nCPAP because a severe mixed SAHS was diagnosed, and concludes that on diagnosing SAHS with an obstructive component there is no primary need for a pacemaker.

governanceNotes: D1 batch 84 (2026-09-27): three bounded associations authored in draft quarantine, following the phantom-limb-pain, scleritis, and salivation precedents. sick-sinus-syndrome is a cardiovascular-expansion-wave-3 identity with no registered incoming edge from any conduction-system disorder before this batch; cardiac-arrhythmia carried 14 incoming edges and cerebrovascular-accident-stroke-residuals 10, none from a sinus node disorder, while dizziness carried only 2, from inappropriate-sinus-tachycardia and orthostatic-hypotension, making dizziness the genuinely thin target.

MEchanism note: NEUROLOGICAL_DEGENERATION is used for the rhythm and dizziness edges to name the shared age-related fibroelastic replacement of the sinus node and conduction tissue, and the rank 1 edge records the located randomised trial as an EXPLICIT COUNTERWEIGHT because it is a NEGATIVE trial for atrial pacing minimisation reducing atrial fibrillation, so the mechanism cannot be stated as simple pacing-induced. THROMBOTIC_OR_VASCULAR is used for the stroke edge and is a good fit, with the located UK Biobank analysis interpreting its isolated-sinus-node-dysfunction finding as evidence of a left atrial myopathy rather than a demonstrated embolic lesion.

RANK ORDER IS EVIDENCE-LED AND CONTRARY TO CLINICAL PROMINENCE, which is deliberate. The dizziness edge is the one a clinician would name first, since it is the presenting symptom, but its primary anchor is a single-arm before-and-after study in which every patient received a pacemaker and whose authors state that no causal relationship could be established, and its second anchor is a review authored in part by the device manufacturer's employees, and its third is a single-patient case report. Ranking it above the stroke and rhythm edges would have presented the weakest evidence in the file as its headline claim.

WITHHELD ROUTES: syncope as EVIDENCE-INSUFFICIENT, because the located anchors address syncope as a safety endpoint of pacing programming (PMID 37638973), as a device effect on reflex syncope (PMID 40388576), or as a symptom in a single case (PMID 19156381), and no anchor quantifies syncope as a complication of sinus node disease in an unselected untreated population. implantable-cardiac-pacemaker as TREATMENT-CONSEQUENCE rather than a medical secondary condition, every located anchor being about implantation decisions or post-implantation outcomes rather than about a condition the disease produces. heart-block as SCOPE-OVERLAP and DIFFERENTIAL, the located literature treating atrioventricular nodal block as a distinct conduction disorder that coexists with and is named separately from sinus node disease (PMID 40607080), so the two should not be merged into one route. atrial-flutter as MISSING IDENTITY, no catalog identity existing for it. The catalog's sibling inappropriate-sinus-tachycardia was left untouched per the standing rule on shared pacing substrate, the located review naming both as contributors to the same overlap phenotype rather than one causing the other.
